domain: Education Policy / Constitutional Law / Social Stratification
topic_summary: Analysis of affirmative action in university admissions, examining race-conscious admissions policies as mechanisms for addressing historical exclusion and present-day inequality. The topic centers on the collision between remedial justice frameworks, meritocratic selection norms, and constitutional equal protection doctrine following recent Supreme Court decisions.

key_entities: Applicant populations (stratified by race, class, legacy status)
Supreme Court (constitutional adjudicator; recent SFFA decisions)
Historical exclusion systems (Jim Crow, redlining, school segregation)
key_tensions: Remedial justice vs formal equality (race-conscious correction vs colorblind doctrine)
Individual merit vs group representation (selection by achievement vs demographic targets)
Educational mission vs stratification reproduction (diversity goals vs legacy/wealth advantages)
key_mechanisms: Race-conscious admissions (explicit consideration of racial identity in holistic review)
Legacy preferences (admissions advantage for children of alumni)
Standardized testing (SAT/ACT as purportedly neutral sorting mechanism)
key_absences: Class-based affirmative action as structural alternative
Wealth transfer mechanisms underlying legacy admissions and test prep access

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Equal Protection Clause of the 14th Amendment as constitutional constraint on state action regarding racial classification
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Supreme Court interpretive supremacy over constitutional meaning; judicial review doctrine

readings.commitment: Equal protection permits race-conscious remedies for documented historical exclusion
readings.authority_grounding: Substantive equality tradition; Bakke diversity rationale; remedial justice framework
readings.expected_structural_delta: Universities as beneficiaries (mission autonomy); excluded groups enter beneficiary set; formal equality norm becomes victim of remedial override

readings.commitment: Equal protection forbids any racial classification by state actors absent compelling interest
readings.authority_grounding: Formal equality tradition; originalist interpretation; SFFA v. Harvard/UNC holdings
readings.expected_structural_delta: Rejected applicants (particularly Asian-American) enter victim set; universities lose mission autonomy; meritocracy norm becomes beneficiary

readings.commitment: Equal protection forbids systems that perpetuate caste-like subordination of historically excluded groups
readings.authority_grounding: Critical race theory; structural inequality tradition; group-harm focus
readings.expected_structural_delta: Legacy preferences and wealth-gated access enter victim set; subordinated groups become primary beneficiaries; formal neutrality claims become snares

axiom_contradictions.basis: Remedial reading holds that equal protection permits race-consciousness to correct historical exclusion; colorblind reading holds that equal protection forbids race-consciousness except in narrowest circumstances. No single framework can hold both that the Constitution permits and forbids the same classification simultaneously.

Colorblind reading treats formal neutrality as constitutional mandate; antisubordination reading treats formal neutrality as constitutional violation when it perpetuates subordination. No framework can hold both that neutrality satisfies and violates equal protection simultaneously.

axes.selection_reason: Kernel reading with distinct authority grounding and victim structure

axes.selection_reason: Kernel reading with distinct structural focus and victim set (includes legacy preferences)

axes.human_readable: Meritocracy Measurement Instability (Test Score as Proxy)

axes.primary_observable: SAT/ACT score correlation with household income; test prep industry revenue; score variance by race/class
axes.selection_reason: Independent observable (test score validity); distinct beneficiary structure; surfaces hidden extraction in meritocracy claims

axes.primary_observable: Legacy admit rates vs general admit rates; alumni donation correlation with legacy preference strength; demographic composition of legacy admits
axes.selection_reason: Independent observable (legacy admit advantage); distinct from test score axis; surfaces wealth transfer mechanism absent from affirmative action debate

axes.structural_delta: Shift from remedial justice justification to educational benefit justification for race-conscious admissions following Bakke
axes.primary_observable: Judicial doctrine evolution from Bakke to Grutter to SFFA; university mission statements; empirical studies on diversity outcomes
axes.selection_reason: Independent observable (justification framework shift); rope coordination problem; distinct from kernel readings

omegas.description: Would class-based affirmative action (income/wealth targeting) achieve similar demographic outcomes without triggering strict scrutiny? Absence in extraction suggests structural blind spot.
Do international students (often full-pay) function as revenue extraction mechanism that subsidizes domestic financial aid? If so, meritocracy claims may obscure fiscal dependency.

Are there additional live readings of the Equal Protection kernel beyond the three identified (e.g., libertarian non-interference reading, communitarian group-rights reading)? Reading set may be incomplete.
Why do legacy preferences not trigger equal protection scrutiny despite functioning as wealth-based classification? Legal doctrine gap or interpretive capture?
